source_en: Delivering a shipment of timber to the city yards.
Buying supplies. Twice a season, as always.
Buying winter grain for a small livestock plot.
Seeking iron traps to catch the "things" in the mist.
Trading wolf pelts for clean water filters.
Buying lamp oil. The fog comes lower every night.
The tree line is dead. I came for a roof.
Looking for solid shelter. The sky is watching.
Nothing grows past the north gate. I need food.
Going to my office job at the city planning bureau.
Picking up my wife and kids from school.
Moving into a city flat. I never liked the forest.
Selling my cabin. I have never lived outside the city.
Asking the way to the north gate. Never been past it.
Hiring a guide to teach me how to track animals.
Selling fresh mushrooms from the forest. Good harvest.
Going to the cinema with my neighbours from the block.
Hosting a dinner party for my friends tonight.
Papers. Fresh from the envelope.
The birds left the valley this morning. They know before we do.
I am here for supplies. The trees are starting to taste like copper.
You have a shadow following you that doesn't match your feet, officer.
The fog is getting teeth. I need to get back to my cabin before it bites.
Take the form. The ink smells like old blood today.
The forest is gone. It didn't die; it just... left.
I don't need a name anymore. The wind doesn't use them.
I am going to find a cave. The sky is looking for us.
Stay quiet. Listen to the wind.
Watch your back, officer. The walls are getting thin.
Bury your heart deep. It’s the only way to keep it.
A cage is just a smaller forest. I will wait.
I can smell the rot in these walls. It’s older than you.
Lock the door. It won't help, but it feels better.
The... predator... finally... wins...
I return... to the... earth...
The hunt... is... over.
A den. I have slept in worse.
The scent in here is wrong. But I have endured worse smells.
Watch the door. Things follow you more than you think they do.
Back to the roots… back to the dark soil… This is… correct.
The predator… always finds you… in the end…
Tell the forest… nothing has been wasted… I will feed it…
Where are you coming from?
The northern forest. Timber for the city yards. Twice a season, same as always.
My cabin past the north gate. The fog comes lower every night. I need iron traps. Wire does not hold.
The tree line. What is left of it. Nothing grows there now. I came for a roof.
The southern orchards. I pick apples on the kolkhoz there. Never cared much for the forest.
My flat in block seven. My wife keeps it warm. I only go out to the woods on Sundays.
The forest. It is green and full. The birds came back to the valley this week.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
No. Sap on my hands. Smoke in my chest. Same as every winter.
Stiff joints in the mornings. The cold, maybe. I do not sleep much. I listen instead.
Dry skin. Cracked at the knuckles. The air does it. I do not complain.
Nothing. At fifty a man knows his own body. Mine is fine.
Nothing. I sleep sound. The neighbours in the next cabin keep watch on the tree line for me.
Nothing. My hands are soft. I sit at a desk in the forestry office all day.
The birds left the valley this morning. They know before we do.
The wind is coming from the wrong direction today. Watch yourself.
Something has been moving in the tree line. Nothing I recognize.
You have a shadow that does not match your feet, officer. Be careful.
The fog is getting teeth. I need to get back before dark.
Take the form. The ink smells like old blood today.
The forest did not die. It left. You do not understand what that means yet.
The sky is looking for us. Stay under something solid.
Everything that was green is gone. That is all I will say.
